claims.text: A ServiceAccount is a namespaced object that provides an identity for processes running in Pods (programs), as opposed to user accounts for people.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Security > Service Accounts (What are service accounts?)

claims.text: Kubernetes creates a ServiceAccount named default in every namespace; a Pod that sets no serviceAccountName is assigned default (by the ServiceAccount admission controller) when it is created.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Security > Service Accounts (Default service accounts); Reference > Admission controllers (ServiceAccount)

claims.text: Unless automountServiceAccountToken is false, a token for the Pod's ServiceAccount is mounted in each container under /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/, with files token, ca.crt and namespace.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Configure Service Accounts for Pods (Opt out of API credential automounting); Accessing the API from a Pod; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt

claims.text: The kubelet obtains the token from the API server for the Pod and refreshes the mounted token file before the token expires.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > Managing Service Accounts (Bound service account tokens; kubelet proactively rotates the token)

claims.text: A ServiceAccount token is a signed credential (a JWT signed by the API server's service account signing key) naming one ServiceAccount; the API server verifies it during authentication.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > Access Authn Authz > Authenticating (Service account tokens: signed bearer tokens / JWT)

claims.text: A ServiceAccount authenticates with user name system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name> and groups system:serviceaccounts and system:serviceaccounts:<namespace>, plus system:authenticated, the group of every caller that passed authentication.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Authenticating (Service account tokens); Using RBAC Authorization (Referring to subjects); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt

claims.text: A ServiceAccount's request is authenticated and authorized like a person's kubectl request; RBAC lets it do only what bindings naming it or its groups allow, and refuses anything else with 403 Forbidden.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Using RBAC Authorization (Referring to subjects; Service account permissions); Controlling Access to the Kubernetes API

claims.text: Default RBAC binds no rights on objects of user namespaces to service accounts outside kube-system; via system:authenticated they only get read-only discovery and self-information, so default may not list pods, get secrets or create deployments.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Using RBAC Authorization (Service account permissions; Default roles and role bindings: system:basic-user, system:discovery); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt

claims.text: The API server authenticates a request by the bearer token it carries, not by its origin: the token read from with-token works from the host with kubectl --token.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Authenticating (Service account tokens can be used outside the cluster); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt

claims.text: automountServiceAccountToken: false in a Pod's spec keeps the token from being mounted; the Pod still runs as its ServiceAccount (default when none is named).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Configure Service Accounts for Pods (Opt out of API credential automounting)

claims.text: Opinion: when a program never calls the API server, turn off the token mount, because anyone who reads the file gets the ServiceAccount's rights.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Security > Service Accounts / RBAC Good Practices (opt out of automounting tokens)

claims.text: kubectl get serviceaccounts shows SECRETS 0 for default because tokens are no longer auto-generated as Secrets; Pods get tokens requested by the kubelet.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Managing Service Accounts (Auto-generated legacy ServiceAccount token clean up; Bound service account tokens); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-accounts.txt
